## Student downloads

[Download the HTML website, student RStudio project, or PDF bundle](downloads.qmd). The RStudio package includes the lesson sources, exercises, teaching CSVs, required assets, and setup instructions.

## Teaching datasets

Use the [checked textbook CSV bundle](../data/module02/descriptive-statistics-data.zip) for the active descriptive-statistics lessons. The [data guide](../data/module02/README.md) explains columns, units, sources, and verification limits.

The supplementary [student age and height CSV](../data/module02/student_age_height.csv) supports histogram interpretation. Read its [source and metadata limitations](../data/module02/student-age-height-notes.md) before using it.

The [measure-limitations examples](../data/module02/measure_limitations_examples.csv) accompany Lesson 3. Their [provenance notes](../data/module02/measure-limitations-source-notes.md) distinguish instructor examples and original teaching illustrations.

## Probability model inputs

[Module 3](../modules/03-probability-and-distributions/index.qmd) reuses the Restaurant CSV for finite-selection probabilities. Its later lessons enter explicitly cited aggregate counts and model parameters from the textbook directly in R. No individual daily-sales, customer, arrival-time, flight, or tire records are supplied or invented. Simulation outputs are artificial draws under a stated model.

## Working with the course

Follow the numbered modules from the [course home](../index.qmd). Lessons, practice, and the integrated review appear in their teaching order. Instructor answers stay separate.

The student project README explains setup and rendering. The full source repository also includes syllabi under `syllabi/`. The instructor maintains a local-only `books/` collection of textbook PDFs and original publisher workbooks, and local guidance under `docs/`; those folders are excluded from GitHub and are not needed to use the supplied teaching CSVs.
